title: Man found guilty after fatally shooting 17-year-old in Woodbridge - NewsBreak
text: PRINCE WILLIAM COUNTY, Va. ( DC News Now ) — A years-long investigation came to a close Tuesday after a jury found a 23-year-old man guilty of the murder of a teenager. Prince William County Commonwealth’s Attorney Amy Ashworth said the charges against Jordan Sickels stem from a robbery and deadly shooting on Aug. 12, 2023. On that day, the Prince William County Police Department (PWCPD) was called to a community pool in Woodbridge after receiving reports of a shooting. There, they found 17-year-old Roberto Martinez Inglis. He had been shot in his head and hand. Investigators said they found security footage from the pool, which showed two cars entering the parking lot before the shooting broke out. Three suspects got out of one of the cars and entered the second car, which Martinez Inglis was driving. After a few minutes, the footage showed a shot going through the front windshield, and the three suspects returning to their car before speeding away from the scene. PWCPD said Sickels and two other suspects planned on selling a gun to Martinez Inglis. During the transaction, however, Sickels robbed the teenager and shot him. Police found blood-stained money while executing a search warrant during the investigation, officials noted. “My heart goes out to the family and friends of Roberto Martinez Inglis, the 17-year-old who was murdered by the Defendant. While this verdict is an important step in holding the Defendant accountable, it does nothing to alleviate the pain of losing a son, brother, grandson, nephew, cousin, uncle, and friend. Now that the trial is over, we will focus on getting a sentence that is fair and just,” Ashworth said in a news release. Sickels was convicted on June 17 of second-degree murder, robbery resulting in death and use of a firearm in commission of a felony. He is scheduled to be sentenced on Oct. 10.
